title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate‑Verify‑Repair for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents, 400 paired episodes) to evaluate whether a deterministic verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM produces device configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by both baseline and guarded). Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.02; preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (primary confirmatory test). An exploratory paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04]. Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All reported numeric values, provider‑call accounting, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived execution and analysis bundle. We interpret the preregistered confirmatory result conservatively and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limits and operational implications.

sections.introduction:
Automating the translation of high‑level operator intent into device configuration scripts is an active NetOps research direction because it promises to reduce routine operator labor and speed maintenance workflows. However, large language models (LLMs) can produce mechanically detectable faults—syntax errors, topology/reachability violations, and ACL/policy mistakes—that have direct operational consequences such as availability loss or unintended access changes. Prior prototype work documents these error modes and advocates verifier‑guided repair loops as a mitigation pattern [1]–[3].

This paper reports a preregistered, provenance‑traced paired experiment that measures the effect of a deterministic verifier plus a bounded repair budget on mechanically detectable policy violations in an emulator. We focus on operationally meaningful error classes that a deterministic verifier can express (syntactic validity, required‑command sequencing, reachability/topology constraints, and encoded ACL/policy checks). The experiment uses a paired design with shared_initial_candidate sampling semantics so that, for each operator intent, baseline and guarded outcomes start from the identical sampled draft configuration; any paired difference therefore arises only from deterministic validator/repair activity and not from independent first‑pass sampling or alternate prompting. Our preregistered primary estimand compares the probability of zero detected violations under guarded (GVR) versus baseline (single‑shot) generation using an exact McNemar two‑sided test.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and domain reviews document rapid growth in LLM applications for NetOps and AIOps while noting recurring evaluation gaps: lack of provenance, sparse verifier integration, and limited multi‑vendor emulation evidence [5], [6]. Prototype NetOps studies show that LLMs can draft device configurations or configuration‑like artifacts but often introduce syntax, topology, or policy errors; verifier‑guided repair has been demonstrated as an empirically supported mitigation across adjacent domains (code, domain‑specific programs) [2], [3], [4].

Those prior demonstrations establish two important points that motivate our design: (i) a deterministic verifier must be able to mechanize domain rules and provide localized diagnostics to enable targeted repairs; and (ii) evaluation must pair generator outputs with deterministic checking under provenance tracing so that outcomes and costs (model calls) are auditable. Existing work is largely prototype‑scale, often single‑vendor or single‑device, and typically mixes generation and verification artifacts without a preregistered paired design—gaps this study aims to reduce by using a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory protocol across heterogeneous template families in an emulator.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: We preregistered study C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 before any model calls. The preregistration specified a single primary estimand: the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, evaluated with an exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary per‑intent success indicators (success = no operationally detectable policy violations after the applicable pipeline completes). The preregistration SHA‑256 is 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50.

Sampling, strata, and shared_initial_candidate semantics: The confirmatory sample was N = 200 unique operator intents chosen deterministically from a frozen task index and stratified across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns (12 strata total). The experiment was executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial generation was sampled (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1) and that same generated candidate was reused by both the baseline and guarded episodes. The preregistration explicitly declared that independent constrained‑prompt arms were not executed; consequently observed paired differences can originate only from deterministic validator/repair actions that are permitted in the guarded pipeline.

Model, sampling remarks, and budget: The archived execution manifest records the declared model as gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses) and an archived model_configuration that lists temperature = null/unset. We state explicitly that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The preregistered model‑call budget was maximum_model_calls = 400, with maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The run used no retrieval augmentation.

Deterministic validator and guarded policy: The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implements (a) syntactic parsing and canonicalization of generated commands, (b) required‑command sequencing checks against the task payload's required_sequence, (c) reachability/topology checks by simulating the resulting device state in the Mininet emulation, and (d) encoded ACL/policy checks derived from the task constraints. Scoring followed the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: an episode is scored as success only when the validator reports zero violations after finalization. The guarded pipeline invoked at most one verifier‑triggered repair call per intent; a repair call was submitted only when the validator returned violations and the repair prompt included the validator's localized diagnostics.

Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation: The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation files record complete episode accounting: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, complete_pair_count = 200, and hosted_model_call_event_count = 204. Stage decomposition audited 200 shared_initial_generation events and 4 repair calls (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 4). Cache statistics show cache_hit_count = 0 and cache_miss_count = 204. These audited counts are used verbatim in the Results section for arithmetic derivations (mean extra calls per intent, calls per avoided violation). All numerical run and analysis artifacts cited in this paper are drawn from the archived execution and analysis bundle.
sections.results:
Execution outcomes and contingency counts: The run completed as preregistered (complete_pair_count = 200). The paired contingency table extracted from analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv is: n11 = 196 (success in both conditions), n10 = 4 (guarded success, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (guarded fail, baseline success), n00 = 0 (both fail). From these counts baseline success rate = 196/200 = 0.98 and guarded success rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.02.

Confirmatory test and exploratory interval: The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test computed on the paired binary outcomes yielded p = 0.125 (the preregistered primary confirmatory result; we do not reject at α = 0.05). As a preregistered exploratory descriptor, a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) for the paired risk difference produced a 95% CI = [0.005, 0.04]. We emphasize that the exact McNemar p‑value is the formal preregistered inferential result and that the bootstrap interval is exploratory magnitude context.

Repair invocation and cost accounting: Four verifier‑triggered repairs were invoked across the 200 intents; total hosted model calls recorded = 204 (200 shared initial + 4 repairs). From these audited numbers we compute mean hosted model calls per intent = 204 / 200 = 1.02; mean extra calls per intent attributable to guarded repairs = 0.02; and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0 (four repairs correspond to four baseline failures corrected under the guarded pipeline). These arithmetic values are taken directly from the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation artifacts and are reported here to permit independent reconciliation with the archived bundle.

Representative trace diagnostics: Representative validator traces and response artifacts show the same shared initial candidate file content was used by both baseline and guarded episodes for each pair (shared_initial_candidate semantics). In the four discordant pairs the validator produced localized violation diagnostics that triggered repair prompts; each repair resulted in a corrected final configuration that passed the deterministic validator. The archived scoring records mark these episodes with score_reason_code = VALID_CONFIGURATION after repair and record validator_trace.repair_applied = true for repaired episodes.

Statistical diagnostics and power considerations: Discordant pair count (n10 + n01 = 4) is small, which limits power to detect small absolute differences and can render resampling‑based intervals sensitive to sampling variability. In sparse‑discordance settings exact conditional tests (McNemar) should be prioritized for confirmatory inference; bootstrap percentile intervals can be informative about magnitude but may be unstable when discordant counts are small. We therefore rely on the exact McNemar result (p = 0.125) as the formal preregistered inference and present the bootstrap CI only for effect‑size context.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory interpretation and scope: The preregistered exact McNemar test did not reject at α = 0.05, so the confirmatory protocol does not provide statistically significant evidence (by that threshold) that guarded GVR improves the paired zero‑violation probability in this workload. Nevertheless the observed point estimate (0.02) and the exploratory bootstrap CI ([0.005, 0.04]) indicate a small positive effect size with low absolute baseline failure prevalence (2%), and the audited provider accounting shows that a minimal repair budget (4 repairs) sufficed to correct all mechanically detectable baseline violations in this emulated workload.

Construct validity and verifier coverage: A central limitation is construct coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 checks syntactic correctness, required‑command sequencing, reachability/topology consequences in the Mininet emulator, and encoded ACL/policy predicates present in the task payload. The validator cannot detect higher‑order semantic misinterpretations or specification mismatches that are not expressible in its rule set. Thus a guarded pass that is marked valid by the validator may still conceal semantic errors outside the verifier's coverage; expanding the verifier ontology remains necessary to reduce such residual false negatives.

Internal validity and shared_initial_candidate implications: Because the experiment used shared_initial_candidate semantics and exactly one initial generation per intent was sampled (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1), baseline outcomes represent the validator score on that shared draft; guarded outcomes represent the final pipeline result after deterministic validation and at most one permitted repair. This design isolates the effect of validator/repair activity: any paired improvement derives from deterministic repair activity rather than differences in initial generation sampling or alternate prompt templates. We explicitly note that independent constrained‑prompt arms were not executed and therefore the study does not estimate effects attributable to alternative prompting or independent multi‑sample generation.

Operational implications and bounded claims: Within the constrained Mininet emulation, synthetic provenance‑traced templates, and the verifier rule set, a very small repair budget eliminated the observed mechanically detectable baseline violations with minimal model‑call overhead. This suggests that, when a deterministic verifier can express relevant constraints and provide localized diagnostics, modest repair budgets can materially reduce mechanically checkable faults in template‑driven emulated workloads. We do not claim production readiness, multi‑model generality, or coverage for semantic errors outside the validator's rules.

Reproducibility and archived artifacts: All numeric counts and analysis artifacts reported above are reproduced verbatim from the archived execution and analysis bundle. The preregistration record, execution manifest (including hosted_model_call audit), deterministic_reconciliation, analysis CSVs (paired_contingency_table.csv and condition_summary.csv), and representative validator traces are archived and together substantiate the contingency counts, repair accounting, and provider_call decomposition reported in this manuscript. The preregistration SHA‑256 and the immutable initial master‑prompt locator are provided in the Disclosure Statement below to permit independent audit of the preregistration and initial prompting constraints.

Recommendations and future work grounded in artifacts: (1) Increase deterministic verifier coverage to encode additional semantic and policy ontologies and quantify residual false negatives; (2) execute paired designs with independent multi‑sample initial generations to measure effects attributable to constrained prompting or alternate initial prompts (not executed here); (3) evaluate multiple hosted models and model versions to assess robustness to provider nondeterminism; (4) preserve provenance tracing for all provider calls and validator traces to support independent replication and audit. Each recommendation follows directly from observed artifact evidence and listed limitations.
sections.conclusion:
We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents; shared_initial_candidate semantics) that evaluated whether a deterministic verifier plus bounded repair reduces mechanically detectable policy violations for intent‑to‑configuration tasks in a Mininet emulation. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.125). Guarded GVR invoked four repairs and corrected the four observed baseline violations at low model‑call overhead (mean extra calls per intent = 0.02), yielding a paired risk difference estimate of 0.02 and an exploratory paired bootstrap CI = [0.005, 0.04] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). These artifact‑grounded results indicate that, for template‑driven emulated workloads where a deterministic verifier can express and check relevant constraints and provide localized feedback, a small repair budget can eliminate mechanically detectable policy violations. The results do not establish production readiness, multi‑model generality, or coverage for semantic errors outside the verifier; future preregistered, provenance‑traced evaluations should expand verifier coverage and test multiple models.

limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not generalize directly to production hardware or live operations.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); higher‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from verifier‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α = 0.05 for N = 200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduced power to detect small absolute improvements under some preregistered scenarios.
